title: THE CAUSES, BASES, AND SOURCES OF ILLUSION

lists.name: ILLUSIONS
lists.of: bases, sources, or causes of illusion
items: Overgeneralization, Exaggeration, Infinitization, Absolutization, Non-qualification, Eternalization, Idealization, etc.
Erroneous substitution of part for whole.
Excessive abstraction, Theoretical fictions, Neglect of concrete facts.
Logical fallacies, Misapplication of general principles.
Lack of self-criticism, Self-ignorance, Lack of criticism in general.
Unconstrained imagination, 'Pseudo-perception' (spurious acts of perception that are assumed to have occurred but that in fact did not occur).

Ignorance about illusion in general: its diversity, categories, taxa, omnipresence, signs, causes, genesis, laws, instances and spectrum of exemplifications, transformations, transcendence, degrees, related phenomena, powers, etc.
Neglect of scientific procedures: testing, experimentation, prediction, validation, reproduction, statistical evaluation, induction, deduction, rich hypothetication, etc.
Neuropsychological heredity: e.g. inherited modes, gestalten, or elements of perception, thought, feeling, or action.
Random patterns, Coincidences, Juxtapositions, and 'Background noise'.
Neurosis, Psychosis, Other forms of irrationality.
Psychophysical boundary values, Objective similarity, Non-discrimination, Under-differentiation, Mis-analogy.
Information overload, Mental or Perceptual fatigue, 'Environmental burial'.
Hierarchy (multiplicity of confusable and interfering levels).
Misconstrual of function from appearance, Mis-supposition of appearance from function.
Poor or defective correlation of data, Mis-combined sensa or Percepts.

notes: total items: 76. 1984 Mr 24. NOTE: These are the most common, important, or distinct bases, sources, or causes of illusion (of illusions in general). The photograph cuts off the second page after item 49.
